plans.note: Section 21 has a mutual cap at greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, a consequential-damages exclusion with direct-damage clarifications, and Excluded Claims for confidentiality, data protection, security, indemnities, gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud and IP. Check cap adequacy and that Customer's payment obligation carve-out (21.3) is not asymmetric against us. Cross-ref insurance non-limitation in 18.2 and 21.4 survival language.

Vendor IP indemnity in 20.1 and conduct-based indemnity in 20.2; Customer's reciprocal indemnity in 20.3 is narrow with exclusions. Verify procedure in 20.4 (control of defence, settlement consent) and infringement remedies in 20.5, cross-referenced by termination right 9.3. Confirm indemnities are Excluded Claims under 21.3.

12.3 expressly preserves Customer freedom to build, buy and compete and disclaims non-compete/MFN/no-hire commitments. Check for tension with sec-2.2 (exclusivity) which is a separate rule; only flag here if a genuine restriction on our lines of business exists.

sec-2.2 (first of two clauses numbered 2.2) makes Vendor the sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services — a direct hit against this rule, notwithstanding the contrary disclaimers in 2.1 and 12.3. Note the internal conflict when redlining.

sec-7.2 (first clause numbered 7.2) obliges Customer to give Vendor terms no less favourable than those offered any other technology supplier — an MFN running against us. 12.3 disclaims any MFN commitment; flag the conflict. Do not confuse with the invoicing clause at sec-7.2-2.

12.4 binds Customer for eighteen months post-termination, covers anyone employed by Vendor at any time during the term, bars engagement as well as solicitation, and has no general-advertising carve-out. Compare 12.3's general-recruitment freedom language.

Section 9 contains only for-cause, insolvency and Customer-specific cause triggers; no convenience termination right for Customer appears anywhere (check 8.1-8.2 term/renewal and 27.3 force-majeure exit before concluding). If missing, propose Customer-only convenience termination on notice with pro-rata refund per 10.2.

8.2 auto-renews twelve months with a 180-day non-renewal notice window (long); 8.3 caps uplift at lesser of CPI and 3% with 90 days' notice, which is favourable. Assess the notice window against the playbook parameter; do not flag the uplift cap.

28.1 selects New York law with CISG excluded; 28.2 gives exclusive jurisdiction to New York County courts with an injunctive-relief carve-out; 28.3 adds an executive escalation that does not block urgent relief. Appears within accepted parameters.

24.1 permits Customer assignment to Affiliates/successors without consent; 24.2 restricts Vendor assignment and change of control; 24.4 blocks Vendor termination or repricing on our change of control; 13.3 allows licence transfer per Section 24. Verify 24.3's catch-all does not undercut 24.1.

14.1 confirms Customer ownership of Customer Data and pre-existing IP; 14.2 assigns Deliverables to Customer on creation subject to payment; 14.3 preserves Vendor Technology with a perpetual licence back via 13.2; 14.4 addresses joint IP and feedback. Cross-check definitions 1.3/1.4/1.8 and the no-model-training restriction in 15.1.

13.1 covers Affiliates and contractors for internal business purposes; 13.2 gives a perpetual paid-up licence for delivered Vendor Technology; 13.3 limits revocation/suspension to material uncured breach after notice and cure. Confirm 13.4 restrictions and any suspension rights elsewhere do not make the licence revocable at will.

22.1 lets Vendor audit at any time without notice with remote access to our systems — contrary to the rule. 22.2 and 22.3 are protective (Vendor bears cost absent >5% underpayment, no direct system access, findings are our Confidential Information); note the internal conflict with 22.1 when redlining. Section 23 may also bear on records.

7.6 imposes USD 25,000 per day liquidated damages on Customer for any dependency delay — a penalty running against us with no cap or cure. Check interaction with the liability cap in 21.1 and the dispute-withholding right in 7.3.

19.1-19.3 give services, conformity, malicious-code and compliance warranties; 19.2 runs ninety days for Deliverables and the full subscription term for hosted Services; 19.4 provides re-perform/repair/replace with termination and refund fallback and preserves other remedies. Assess duration and remedy against the parametric thresholds; acceptance remedies in 6.2 are related.

18.1 sets CGL, workers' comp, employer's liability, E&O USD 2M and cyber USD 5M for the term plus one year; 18.2 covers insurer quality, certificates, cancellation notice and non-limitation of liability. Compare limits against playbook minimums.

2.1 expressly states no minimum quantity or purchase commitment and that declining a further Order Form is not a breach; 7.1 bars unlisted minimum-use charges. Likely compliant, but read alongside the exclusivity clause at sec-2.2 which is handled under EXCLUSIVITY.

11.1 gives up to six months' transition assistance at expiring Order Form rates on any termination; 11.2 requires data return within thirty days in machine-readable format with no hostage-taking for fee disputes; 11.3 covers certified deletion. Cross-check 10.1-10.2 (refunds, continuing rights) and 16.5 confidentiality return.
